item.title: Re: SCP-ARK
item.content:encoded:
PM request acknowledged.

T.L. at your service!

+ Here lies crit crit
- Bye bye crit crit

Though I’m not too big of an expert on mountains or caverns, I’d safely assume that it’s natural for there to just be water in those environments. Could you maybe go into explanation for the water dripping via anomalous means part? Like, evidence that the water dripping there deviates from what is standard/normal/what is expected. I can see why the other anomalous aspects of this concept is anomalous, but it’s just on that water dripping from the cavern part that has me doubting.

Another problem I have with this is the part where the Foundation kills off the specimens. I feel like it’s needless animal cruelty/slaughter and a complete waste of valuable information. It also goes against the Foundation’s Ethic Committee’s morals since there’s really no reasonable reason to kill those animals in the first place.

Lastly, you haven’t really provided much on the story you are telling here. What exactly are these Biblical anomalies? What do they have to do with the cavern and how it makes life? There’s also not a very strong link present between the story of Noah’s Ark and the anomalous cavern. Moreover, what is this specific catastrophe the specimen is talking about? Is it on the flood during Noah’s time? Is it a different catastrophe? What’s the story behind the cavern becoming a safe haven for life? What is the mystery in this? What do you want to reveal and leave vague? What do you have planned to bring out the slight creepiness?

Overall, my main concern with this is the lack of detail in the story you are presenting. I think you should try to flesh out the information on what the specimen has to offer to really help implement the creepy and mysterious feel to it, since there is little to no presence of those genres. Maybe try working on a stronger connection between Noah's Ark and the cavern too, and either remove the killing off the specimens part or give a reasonable reason besides "in fear all of them are unnoticeably anomalous" for the Foundation to kill them off.


If you have any questions regarding my critique, please let me know. You are welcome to PM me for another look, or you may follow up with someone from the Butterfly Squad Roster or IRC Chat rooms.

item.title: SCP-ARK
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): (Other: slightly creepy)

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, and then hints at what the greater picture is via an incident

Elevator Pitch: An SCP that bring life via anomalous means, and has ties to the biblical SCP's such as Dr. Clef's Proposal, and 4840

Central Narrative: In simple term's: its Noah's ark, with that SCP twist to it. The ark is buried underneath a mountain, now making it a 'man made cavern'. This cavern is constantly dripping water and once a day, a drop of water turns to blood, and replicates until it turns into two full specimens of a normal animal species: one male and one female. The wooden structure lining the cavern also has incredibly small carvings, that when translated detail animal DNA. The foundation also found the Journal of the supposed builder. It details things like how his people have grown cruel since the passing of their first leader, and how he's been giving instructions to build a vessel in a specific way, with specific wood. Of course the Foundation attempt to replicate this, and when they fail, they do it with wood found in the cavern. Unfortunately the results are horrific, mutated, close-to sarkic versions of normal animals, and soon enough one of the 'non-anomalous' animals from the actual cavern (a male lamb) speaks during a routine inspection, warning the foundation away from their interference. Eventually the Foundation is forced to eliminate their own specimens, and are left to wonder what they should do with the continually produced 'normal' ones.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's short, sweet, and too the point. It tells the story and leaves the mystery. Think of it like a different take on SCP-2000: an anomaly that (for the most part) creates normal life, but the foundation decides to contain it as they understand it even less.
